note: [L] takes the classes as `Lives`/`bake` and the final functions of Lemmas D4 to D6 as the `Income`/`Remainder` data of the supplier, so the setup is the shape of the `advances` statement, not a separate construction.

snippet.text:
advances N p (m : ℕ) : m < N →
    ∀ l u : ℝ, l ≤ u → ∀ Q, Curve (B.a.budget (m+1)) Q (Set.Icc l u) →
      (∀ x∈ Set.Icc l u, Lives B.bake N (m+1) p (Q x) ∧ (Q x).beta ∈ band B.a (m+1)) →
      ∃ T, Curve (B.a.budget m) T (Set.Icc l u) ∧
        ∀ x∈ Set.Icc l u,B.Move N m p (T x) (Q x)

proof_context.conclusion: `advances` produces from a continuous curve `Q` at level `m+1` a continuous curve `T` of class members at level `m` with `B.Move N m p (T x) (Q x)` for every `x`.
